privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.subtitle: Kelora is built to keep your financial life on your own device. This policy explains, plainly, what that means.

body: Kelora is a personal subscription and budget tracker made by NoSky Studios Ltd. It is designed around a simple idea: the details of what you pay for are yours, and they should stay with you.

We do not have accounts. We do not ask you to sign in. We do not run analytics, advertising, or tracking of any kind. The subscriptions, prices, dates, notes, and budgets you enter are stored on your device and are never sent to us.
The rest of this policy explains the few places data does move — always for a feature you chose, and never to a server we control.
Kelora is published by NoSky Studios Ltd (RC 7631695), a company registered in Nigeria ("NoSky Studios", "we", "us", or "our").
This Privacy Policy applies to the Kelora iOS app and its home-screen widgets. For any privacy question, contact us at [privacy@noskystudios.ng](mailto:privacy@noskystudios.ng).
We want to be specific, because "we value your privacy" means little on its own. In Kelora there is:
list: No account and no sign-in. You do not create a profile, and we never ask for your name, email, or phone number to use the app.
No analytics or usage tracking. Kelora contains no analytics, crash-reporting, advertising, or attribution software. We do not measure how you use the app.
No advertising identifiers. Kelora does not request the App Tracking Transparency permission and does not access the device advertising identifier (IDFA).
No selling or sharing of data. We do not sell, rent, or share your personal information, because we do not receive it in the first place.

body: Everything you put into Kelora is stored locally on your device. This includes the subscriptions and merchants you track, their prices, currencies, billing cycles, start and renewal dates, trial periods, price history, reminders, cancellation dates, payment-method labels, categories, tags, notes, budgets, and any custom icons you choose.

The payment-method field is a free-text label only (for example, "Visa ending 1234"). Kelora does not connect to your bank, card, or any financial institution, and it cannot read your real account or card numbers.

This information stays on your device unless you deliberately move it — for example by turning on iCloud backup, exporting a file, or adding a renewal to your calendar. Those choices are described below. Because the data lives on your device, it is also included in your normal device backups (such as an encrypted iPhone or iCloud device backup) that you control through Apple, not through us.

If you scan a receipt or subscription confirmation, or import a statement, spreadsheet, or document, Kelora reads it entirely on your device using Apple's built-in text-recognition technology. The image and the recognised text are processed locally to help fill in a subscription's details.
Scanned images and their contents are not uploaded to us or to any third party.
Kelora works offline for its core features. It makes a small number of optional network requests, only to power specific features, and never to send us your financial data. Here is the complete list:
list: Currency exchange rates. To convert between currencies, Kelora fetches reference rates from ExchangeRate-API (open.er-api.com). The request contains only a currency code (such as "USD"). It does not contain your subscriptions, amounts, or any personal information.

Brand logos and icons. When you add or edit a subscription, Kelora can fetch a brand logo to make it recognisable. To do this it sends a brand name or website domain (guessed from what you are editing) to logo and icon providers — Logo.dev, Brandfetch, and, as a fallback, Google and DuckDuckGo favicon services. If you search for a custom icon, your search term may also be sent to Openverse and Wikimedia Commons image search. These requests contain the brand or search term only — never your prices, dates, or other data.
after: These providers receive only the information described above, as the operators of the services Kelora contacts on your behalf, and their use of it is governed by their own privacy policies: [Logo.dev](https://logo.dev), [Brandfetch](https://brandfetch.com), [Google](https://policies.google.com/privacy), [DuckDuckGo](https://duckduckgo.com/privacy), [Openverse](https://openverse.org), and [Wikimedia](https://foundation.wikimedia.org/wiki/Policy:Privacy_policy). As with any internet request, these providers may receive your device's IP address and standard request information; we do not receive that information and do not combine it with anything about you.
You can avoid these requests by not using logo lookup or icon search and by relying on manual exchange rates, which Kelora supports.

body: Kelora offers an optional backup to your own iCloud Drive. It is turned off by default. If you turn it on, Kelora writes a single backup file into your personal iCloud Drive so you can restore it on your own devices.

This backup lives in your Apple iCloud account, under your control. It is not stored on any NoSky Studios server, and we cannot see or access it. Its handling is subject to [Apple's Privacy Policy](https://www.apple.com/legal/privacy/). You can delete the backup at any time from the Files app or from within Kelora, and you can turn the feature off to stop future backups.

If you enable Calendar Integration, Kelora adds your upcoming renewal dates as events in your own calendar, so you see them alongside the rest of your schedule. These events are written to your device's calendar (and wherever you sync it, such as your iCloud calendar). No server operated by us is involved, and we do not read your calendar.

sections.h: Purchases and the Kelora Pro upgrade
body: Kelora may offer App Store purchases for expanded features. All purchases are handled by Apple through the App Store using your Apple Account.

Payment is processed entirely by Apple. Kelora never sees or receives your card, bank, or payment details. To manage entitlements, the app receives from Apple only the fact that a valid purchase exists — not your identity or payment information. Purchases, renewals, and refunds are governed by Apple's terms and [Apple's Privacy Policy](https://www.apple.com/legal/privacy/).
Kelora asks for a permission only when you use the feature that needs it, and explains why at the moment it asks:
list: Camera — only to scan a receipt or subscription confirmation. Scanning happens on your device.
Photo Library — only so you can pick an image to use as a custom subscription icon.
Calendars — only if you turn on Calendar Integration, to add renewal dates to your own calendar.
Notifications — only to show the reminders you schedule, such as an upcoming renewal or a cancel-by date. These are local notifications generated on your device.
after: Kelora does not request location, microphone, contacts, or tracking permissions. You can review or change any permission at any time in the iOS Settings app.

body: Kelora's reminders are local notifications, scheduled and delivered on your device. Kelora does not use push notifications and does not register your device with any messaging server. We cannot send you messages, and we do not know whether or when a reminder is shown.

Kelora's widgets display a snapshot of your subscriptions and budget — for example the next charge, your monthly total, and how many subscriptions are active. To do this, the app and its widgets share a small snapshot file in a private, on-device storage area reserved for the app. This data never leaves your device.

Kelora is a general-purpose finance tool intended for adults and is not directed to children. We do not knowingly collect personal information from anyone, including children under the age of 13 (or the equivalent minimum age in your country). Because Kelora has no accounts and collects no personal information, there is no such information for us to hold or delete.

Your Kelora data is stored on your device and is protected by the security of iOS, including the device passcode, encryption, and app sandboxing that Apple provides. The free-trial marker is stored in the device Keychain.

Because your data does not sit on our servers, the most important protection is the one you control: keep your device locked with a passcode or biometrics, and keep iOS up to date. No method of storage or transmission is completely secure, but keeping your data on-device removes the large, central target that a cloud database would present.

You decide how long your data is kept, because you hold it. You can edit or delete any subscription, budget, or other entry inside the app at any time. Deleting the Kelora app removes its on-device data from that device.

If you turned on iCloud backup, delete the backup file from your iCloud Drive (via the Files app or from within Kelora) to remove that copy. If you added renewals to your calendar, remove those events from your calendar app. We hold no copy of your data, so there is nothing for you to request from us and nothing for us to delete on your behalf.

Depending on where you live, data-protection laws — such as the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023, the EU and UK General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), and the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA/CPRA) — give you rights over your personal information, including the rights to access, correct, delete, and port it, and to object to certain processing.

Kelora is designed so that you already have these rights directly: your information is on your device, where you can view, change, export, and delete it yourself, at any time, without asking us. We do not collect, store, sell, or share your personal information, and we do not "sell" or "share" it for advertising as those terms are defined under the CCPA.

If you believe we hold personal information about you, or you have a question about your rights, contact us at [privacy@noskystudios.ng](mailto:privacy@noskystudios.ng) and we will respond. You also have the right to lodge a complaint with your local data-protection authority.

Kelora is available worldwide, and your data stays on your device wherever you are. When you use an optional online feature (exchange rates, logo or icon lookup), the request is handled by that third-party provider, which may process it on servers in another country. Those requests contain only the limited information described in the "Network connections" section above.

We may update this Privacy Policy as Kelora evolves or as the law requires. When we do, we will change the "Effective" date at the top of this page and, for significant changes, note them in the app or its release notes. The current version always lives at this address. Continuing to use Kelora after an update means you accept the revised policy.

For any question about this policy or your privacy, reach us at [privacy@noskystudios.ng](mailto:privacy@noskystudios.ng). For general help with the app, contact [appstore@noskystudios.ng](mailto:appstore@noskystudios.ng).
